outages.place: Paraná, including the North, West, Northwest, and other regions
outages.cause: Storms and two F1 tornadoes that damaged the electrical system with strong wind gusts, lightning, and fallen trees, according to Copel, with Simepar confirming the tornadoes
outages.affected: Copel, in a bulletin issued at 7:00 p.m. Brasília time Sunday, Nov 22 (4:00 p.m. CT), as reported by Umuarama News on Sunday and by TNOnline in an article published at 7:26 p.m. Brasília time Sunday (4:26 p.m. CT), said that it had already restored electricity to 98 percent of the consumer units affected by Friday's storms, and that approximately 8,800 consumer units remained without power across Paraná as of 7:00 p.m. Brasília time Sunday. Those reports, citing Copel, said the remaining outages at that bulletin were concentrated in the West (2,700 units), the North (2,200), the Northwest, including Umuarama and neighboring municipalities (1,500), the Southwest (1,100), the East, covering Curitiba, the metropolitan region, and the coast (767), and Centro-Sul (401). Copel said restoration work would continue without interruption until service was fully restored for all remaining customers. No official firm restoration time for all remaining customers was given. An earlier Copel bulletin issued at 12:30 p.m. Brasília time Sunday, Nov 22 (9:30 a.m. CT), as reported by Umuarama News on Sunday, by OBemdito in an article published at 1:06 p.m. Brasília time Sunday (10:06 a.m. CT) and updated at 1:09 p.m. Brasília time Sunday (10:09 a.m. CT), by CBN Curitiba in an article updated at 2:24 p.m. Brasília time Sunday (11:24 a.m. CT), by Tribuna do Interior in an article published at 3:44 p.m. Brasília time Sunday (12:44 p.m. CT), and by Maringá Atual, had said that more than 96.5 percent of the affected consumer units had already been reconnected and that approximately 16,700 consumer units remained without power at that earlier hour, concentrated in the North (about 4,600 units), the West (4,100), the Northwest (about 3,500), the Southwest (about 2,300), the East (about 1,500), and Centro-Sul (568). An earlier Copel bulletin as of 6:30 p.m. Brasília time Saturday, Nov 21 (3:30 p.m. CT), as reported by CGN at 6:47 p.m. Brasília time Saturday (3:47 p.m. CT) and by Folha de Curitiba at 12:05 a.m. Brasília time Sunday, Nov 22 (9:05 p.m. CT Saturday), had said 54,246 consumer units remained without power and that 299,603 units, or 85 percent, had already been reconnected. An earlier noon Saturday Copel bulletin, as reported by Tribuna do Interior at 2:40 p.m. Brasília time Saturday (11:40 a.m. CT), said 80,588 units remained without power at that earlier hour, 273,261 had been restored (77.2 percent), and the peak had been 353,849 units at 8:02 p.m. Brasília time Friday, Nov 20 (5:02 p.m. CT Friday). Simepar confirmed two F1 tornadoes on Friday, Nov 20, one around 3:00 p.m. Brasília time (noon CT Friday) in the Vila Yolanda neighborhood of Foz do Iguaçu and another around 6:00 p.m. Brasília time (3:00 p.m. CT Friday) in Manoel Ribas, with estimated winds of 117 to 180 km/h.
outages.start: Afternoon and evening of Friday, Nov 20, 2026 (Brasília time), when storms and two F1 tornadoes hit Paraná; the peak of 353,849 consumer units was recorded at 8:02 p.m. Brasília time Friday (5:02 p.m. CT Friday), according to Copel's Saturday noon bulletin as reported by Tribuna do Interior
outages.updated: Nov 22, 2026, Copel bulletin issued at 7:00 p.m. Brasília time Sunday (= 4:00 p.m. CT) via Umuarama News on Sunday and TNOnline published 7:26 p.m. Brasília time Sunday (= 4:26 p.m. CT), on approximately 8,800 consumer units remaining without power and 98 percent already restored, with remaining outages concentrated in the West (2,700), North (2,200), Northwest (1,500), Southwest (1,100), East (767), and Centro-Sul (401); earlier 12:30 p.m. Brasília time Sunday Copel bulletin of approximately 16,700 still out and more than 96.5 percent restored, via Umuarama News, OBemdito, CBN Curitiba, Tribuna do Interior, and Maringá Atual; earlier Saturday 6:30 p.m. Brasília time Copel figure of 54,246 still out via CGN and Folha de Curitiba; earlier noon Saturday Copel bulletin via Tribuna do Interior on 80,588 still out and a Friday peak of 353,849 units at 8:02 p.m. Brasília time Friday; Simepar confirmation of two Friday F1 tornadoes in Foz do Iguaçu and Manoel Ribas

outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, including a large-scale attack on Nov 20 and further strikes reported on Nov 21 and into Nov 22
outages.affected: Ukrenergo, as reported by the Kyiv Independent in an article dated 4:08 p.m. Sunday, Nov 22 (8:08 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET), and by NV in an article dated 3:42 p.m. Sunday (7:42 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET), said on Sunday that the electricity-supply situation in Odesa region was extremely difficult after Russian attacks caused serious damage to main power grids, and that repair work was being disrupted by the continued threat of new attacks and by air-raid alerts. Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a Sunday statement reported by the Kyiv Independent and earlier by Ukrinform at 11:05 a.m. EET Sunday (3:05 a.m. CT), by SNN.UA at 10:13 a.m. EET Sunday (2:13 a.m. CT), and by RBC-Ukraine in an article dated 1:30 p.m. EET Sunday (5:30 a.m. CT), said that during the previous day Russia had again attacked energy facilities, and that as of Sunday morning some consumers were without electricity in the Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Odesa, and Kharkiv regions, with the most difficult situation remaining in Odesa region, where a large number of consumers remained without electricity. The ministry and Ukrenergo said that on Sunday morning energy workers had begun partially restoring power to critical-infrastructure facilities in the Odesa area and were working on backup supply schemes, and that the damage was extensive, so full restoration would take time. Vitalii Bunechko, head of the Zhytomyr regional military administration, as reported by Ukrinform at 10:05 a.m. EET Sunday (2:05 a.m. CT), said that over the previous day Russian forces had carried out four drone strikes on energy facilities in Zhytomyr region. No official customer count was given for those regions as a group. Ukrenergo, as reported Saturday evening and Sunday morning by UA.NEWS at 9:23 a.m. EET Sunday (1:23 a.m. CT), and earlier by LB.ua, 24tv, OBOZ.UA, Focus, UNN, and RBC-Ukraine, said that on Sunday, Nov 22, planned electricity outages would be in effect around the clock in parts of the country: hourly outage schedules of 1 to 2.5 groups, or queues, for all categories of consumers, and capacity-restriction schedules for industry, because of the attacks, and that the situation remained difficult in Odesa and Rivne regions. Ukrenergo, as reported by UNN at 4:17 p.m. Sunday, Nov 22 (8:17 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET), said Russian attacks had damaged the main electricity transmission lines that carry power from nuclear power plants to consumers, including networks associated with the transmission of electricity from the South Ukraine Nuclear Power Plant, causing an acute electricity-supply shortage in Odesa and the surrounding areas, and that an exact timeline for fully restoring the power supply had not yet been announced. No official nationwide customer count was given. No official nationwide customer count, and no official change cancelling those Sunday schedules, was found as of 6:00 PM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (2:00 a.m. EET Monday, Nov 23).
outages.updated: Nov 22, 2026, Ukrenergo Sunday update on serious damage to Odesa-area main grids and an extremely difficult supply situation, via the Kyiv Independent 4:08 p.m. Sunday (= 8:08 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET) and NV 3:42 p.m. Sunday (= 7:42 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET); Ukrenergo via UNN 4:17 p.m. Sunday (= 8:17 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET) on damage to main transmission lines from nuclear power plants, including networks associated with the South Ukraine Nuclear Power Plant, and on an acute shortage in Odesa; Energy Ministry Sunday morning update on outages in Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Odesa, and Kharkiv regions, with the most difficult situation remaining in Odesa region, via the Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform 11:05 a.m. EET Sunday (= 3:05 a.m. CT), SNN.UA 10:13 a.m. EET Sunday (= 2:13 a.m. CT), and RBC-Ukraine 1:30 p.m. EET Sunday (= 5:30 a.m. CT); Zhytomyr OVA head Vitalii Bunechko via Ukrinform 10:05 a.m. EET Sunday (= 2:05 a.m. CT); Ukrenergo Sunday all-day schedules of 1 to 2.5 queues, via UA.NEWS 9:23 a.m. EET Sunday (= 1:23 a.m. CT) and Saturday evening reports; rechecked 6:00 PM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (2:00 a.m. EET Monday, Nov 23), no official nationwide customer count and no official cancellation of those Sunday schedules found

outages.place: Odesa and parts of Odesa district
outages.cause: Repeated Russian attacks on high-voltage transmission networks and other energy facilities critical to the region, including a strike on a DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi energy facility on the morning of Nov 20. Ukrenergo said on Sunday, Nov 22, that main power grids had suffered serious damage and that the electricity-supply situation in Odesa and nearby areas was extremely difficult
outages.affected: Ukrenergo, as reported by the Kyiv Independent in an article dated 4:08 p.m. Sunday, Nov 22 (8:08 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET), and by NV in an article dated 3:42 p.m. Sunday (7:42 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET), said the electricity-supply situation in Odesa and nearby areas was extremely difficult because Russian attacks had seriously damaged trunk, or main, power grids, and that the heavy damage made it physically impossible to deliver the needed amount of electricity to consumers. Ukrenergo said this was not only a power shortage but damage to key infrastructure that the city and nearby settlements depend on, that repair work was being complicated by the continued threat of new attacks and by air-raid alerts, which prevent crews from always working continuously, and that the scale of the damage meant fully restoring power would take time. NV, citing Ukrenergo, said energy workers had worked to restore power on the evening and night of Nov 22 and that partial restoration of power supply to critical-infrastructure facilities began in the morning, with backup supply schemes being prepared. NV also reported that DTEK confirmed large-scale destruction now makes it impossible to transmit enough electricity to Odesa and nearby areas. Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa regional military administration, as reported by NV, said electric public transport was not running in Odesa because of the lack of power, that the city had organized buses along parts of tram and trolleybus routes, and that the strikes had also caused water and heating outages, with public water pump stations and water tankers arranged. The Odesa City Council's Department of Education and Science, as reported by NV, by Ukrainska Pravda on Nov 22, and by the Kyiv Independent, said all city schools would switch to remote learning from Nov 23 through Nov 27 because of disruptions to power, heating, and water supply, and that kindergartens would remain open only for the children of critical-infrastructure workers. Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a Sunday morning statement reported by Ukrinform at 11:05 a.m. EET Sunday (3:05 a.m. CT) and by the Kyiv Independent, said Odesa region remained the most difficult, that a significant number of consumers remained without power, and that no official customer count was given. Earlier Friday, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in an official Nov 20 evening statement, said 8,000 families in 21 settlements remained without power after the morning attack; earlier Friday morning, 41,000 households were without power in the Odesa and Rozdilna districts, according to DTEK's press service as reported by Ukrainska Pravda and Ekonomichna Pravda. Ukrenergo, as reported by UNN at 4:17 p.m. Sunday, Nov 22 (8:17 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET), said Russian attacks had damaged the main electricity transmission lines that carry power from nuclear power plants to consumers, including networks associated with the transmission of electricity from the South Ukraine Nuclear Power Plant, that because of the damage to high-voltage networks energy workers were unable to transmit a sufficient amount of electricity to Odesa and nearby settlements, that a significant number of household consumers were still experiencing serious power outages, and that an exact timeline for fully restoring the power supply had not yet been announced. No official Sunday remaining-customer count was found as of 6:00 PM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (2:00 a.m. EET Monday, Nov 23).
outages.updated: Nov 22, 2026, Ukrenergo Sunday statement that Odesa and nearby areas faced an extremely difficult supply situation after serious damage to main power grids, that full restoration would take time, and that air-raid alerts were disrupting repair crews, via the Kyiv Independent 4:08 p.m. Sunday (= 8:08 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET) and NV 3:42 p.m. Sunday (= 7:42 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET), including DTEK's confirmation that enough electricity could not be transmitted, Oleh Kiper on suspended electric transit and water and heating outages, and the Odesa education department on schools moving to remote learning Nov 23–27, also reported by Ukrainska Pravda; Energy Ministry Sunday morning statement that Odesa remained the most difficult and that a significant number of consumers were still without power, via Ukrinform 11:05 a.m. EET Sunday (= 3:05 a.m. CT) and the Kyiv Independent; earlier Friday DTEK remaining 8,000 families after the morning attack and earlier Friday morning 41,000-household figure; Ukrenergo via UNN 4:17 p.m. Sunday (= 8:17 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET) on damage to main transmission lines from nuclear power plants, including networks associated with the South Ukraine Nuclear Power Plant, and on no exact full-restoration timeline yet; rechecked 6:00 PM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (2:00 a.m. EET Monday, Nov 23), no official Sunday remaining-customer count found

outages.cause: Russian attacks that seriously damaged energy equipment in Sarny district. Rivneoblenergo has said hourly outage schedules did not apply in the affected communities because these were emergency outages from the damage
outages.affected: Oleksandr Koval, head of the Rivne regional military administration, as reported by Rivnenski Novyny at 9:17 p.m. EET Sunday, Nov 22 (1:17 p.m. CT), by Rayon.in.ua at 9:20 p.m. EET Sunday (1:20 p.m. CT), and by Ukrinform at 9:55 p.m. EET Sunday (1:55 p.m. CT), said electricity supply had been restored in Sarny district after the Russian attack. Koval, as quoted by Ukrinform and by Censor.NET at 11:10 p.m. EET Sunday (3:10 p.m. CT), said Sarny district had power again, and he credited crews from the substation service, the high-voltage network operations department, and Rivneoblenergo's Sarny section. Rivnenski Novyny noted that as of Sunday morning almost 50 settlements had still been without power because of the attacks. Earlier Sunday afternoon, the Rivne regional military administration, as reported by Rivnenski Novyny at 6:02 p.m. EET Sunday (10:02 a.m. CT), had said electricity supply was being restored gradually in the city of Sarny, but that there was still no information on exact times for a full return of power. Earlier Sunday morning, the Rivne regional military administration, as reported by Rayon.in.ua at 10:25 a.m. EET Sunday (2:25 a.m. CT), said that about 50 settlements in the Sarny area of Rivne region were still without electricity because of damage to energy infrastructure from Russian attacks. No official customer count was given.
outages.start: Evening of Nov 20, 2026 (Kyiv time), according to Rivneoblenergo as reported by Rivnepost and Rivnenski Novyny
outages.etr: Power was restored on Sunday evening, Nov 22, 2026 (Kyiv time), according to Rivne regional military administration head Oleksandr Koval, as reported by Rivnenski Novyny, Rayon.in.ua, and Ukrinform.
outages.updated: Nov 22, 2026, Rivne regional military administration head Oleksandr Koval via Rivnenski Novyny 9:17 p.m. EET Sunday (= 1:17 p.m. CT), Rayon.in.ua 9:20 p.m. EET Sunday (= 1:20 p.m. CT), and Ukrinform 9:55 p.m. EET Sunday (= 1:55 p.m. CT), saying electricity supply had been restored in Sarny district, also reported by Censor.NET at 11:10 p.m. EET Sunday (= 3:10 p.m. CT); earlier Sunday afternoon Rivne regional military administration via Rivnenski Novyny 6:02 p.m. EET Sunday (= 10:02 a.m. CT) on gradual restoration in the city of Sarny; earlier Sunday morning Rivne regional military administration via Rayon.in.ua 10:25 a.m. EET Sunday (= 2:25 a.m. CT) on about 50 settlements in the Sarny area still without power

outages.place: Kurdistan Region, including Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Duhok, Bazian, and Chamchamal
outages.cause: Suspected drone attack on the Khor Mor gas field on the night of Nov 8, 2026, which halted gas production that supplies much of the region's electricity generation. Dana Gas, the field's operator, later said the facility had sustained significant damage and could produce no gas
outages.affected: Kurdistan24, in a Nov 22, 2026 report, said a trilateral meeting of the Kurdistan Regional Government, Iraq's Oil Ministry, and Dana Gas was expected within the next two days to discuss procedures for restarting natural gas production and delivery from the Khor Mor field. A KRG source told Kurdistan24 that a restart depends on Dana Gas obtaining security approval so it can resume operations, and that official results of investigations into the Nov 8 attack had not yet been made public. The same report said the Nov 8 drone attack in Sulaimani province caused a large fire and stopped gas production entirely, with no casualties, and that the stoppage cut 2,500 to 2,800 megawatts of electricity in the Kurdistan Region and reduced power-supply hours by five to six hours a day. That account is consistent with earlier official figures: Al Jazeera, on Nov 9, citing Iraqi and Kurdish officials and the official Iraqi News Agency, said the attack left more than 70 percent of the Kurdish region without power and, citing Omed Ahmed, spokesperson for the KRG Ministry of Electricity, that it suspended gas supply to power plants in Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Bazian, Chamchamal, and Duhok and knocked between 2,500 and 2,800 megawatts off the grid. Rudaw later quoted Ahmed as saying authorities had increased generation from approximately 1,000 megawatts immediately after the attack to 1,550 megawatts, of which 50 megawatts were reserved for essential facilities and factories, leaving 1,500 megawatts for residents and raising daily public electricity supply to six to eight hours; Ahmed said the electricity then available covered only 40 percent of demand, leaving a 60 percent shortfall, and that no date had been established for production to resume. Rudaw's article image assets for that report are dated Nov 13, 2026. 964media, in a Nov 15 report, quoted Ahmed as saying that no timeframe had been set for supplies to return to normal and that within 48 hours of the attack generation had been increased from 1,000 megawatts to nearly 1,650 megawatts. Dana Gas, in a Nov 14 clarification later restated in coverage including a Kurdistan24 report, said the facility had sustained significant damage and that no gas could currently be produced. The Insight International, in a Nov 21 report citing private-generator officials who spoke to Rudaw on Saturday, Nov 21, said the public grid remained weak because of the gas shortfall and that neighborhood generators were still running for most of the day in Erbil, Sulaimani, and Duhok. No official customer count was given. No later official ministry generation figure, and no official confirmation that Khor Mor production had resumed, was found as of 6:00 PM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (2:00 a.m. Iraq time Monday, Nov 23).
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. A KRG source told Kurdistan24 on Nov 22 that a restart depends on Dana Gas obtaining security approval, and that a meeting on restart procedures was expected within two days; as of the latest official statements found, no date had been established for Khor Mor production to resume.
outages.updated: Nov 22, 2026, Kurdistan24 on a planned trilateral meeting within two days on restarting Khor Mor production, with a KRG source saying a restart depends on Dana Gas obtaining security approval, and on the field remaining shut after the Nov 8 attack that cut 2,500 to 2,800 megawatts and reduced supply hours by five to six hours a day; earlier Al Jazeera Nov 9 citing Iraqi and Kurdish officials and INA; KRG electricity ministry figures via Rudaw (article image assets dated Nov 13) and 964media Nov 15; Dana Gas still-shut statement of Nov 14; The Insight International Nov 21, citing private-generator officials who spoke to Rudaw on Saturday, Nov 21, on the public-grid shortfall continuing; rechecked 6:00 PM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (2:00 a.m. Iraq time Monday, Nov 23), no later official generation figure or confirmation that Khor Mor production had resumed found

outages.place: Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Yenakiieve, Debaltseve, Torez, Snizhne, and nearby districts
outages.cause: A massive attack on energy infrastructure on the night of Nov 22, 2026, according to occupation government head Andrei Chertkov, who said new outages were added to the effects of earlier damage; earlier official accounts had also described local accidents, a power deficit, and network overloads
outages.affected: Occupation government head Andrei Chertkov, as reported by DNR News at 5:45 p.m. Sunday, Nov 22 (8:45 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said restoration of the damaged energy center would take a long period, roughly two to three weeks. According to that report, citing Chertkov, a transformer could be installed and connected at the damaged facility within three to four days, but could be damaged again within five days because of repeated attacks on the same centers, and organizing passive protection, along with demining, would also take time. No later official region-wide remaining-customer total was given in that afternoon report. Earlier Sunday morning, Chertkov, as reported by Kommersant at 11:34 a.m. Sunday (2:34 a.m. CT if Moscow time), by DNR News at 11:15 a.m. Sunday (2:15 a.m. CT if Moscow time), by NEWS.ru at 11:25 a.m. Sunday (2:25 a.m. CT if Moscow time), by Moscow 24 at 11:14 a.m. Sunday (2:14 a.m. CT if Moscow time), and by Vedomosti, said that after a massive overnight attack on energy facilities, electricity supply had been disrupted across a large part of the occupied Donetsk region and that more than 279,000 subscribers remained without electricity. Those morning reports, citing Chertkov, said that as of Sunday morning, Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Yenakiieve, Debaltseve, Torez, and Snizhne were partially without power, and that outages were also reported in settlements in the Volnovakha, Amvrosiivka, Telmanove, Yasynuvata, and Volodarske municipal districts, a total of 12 municipalities. Chertkov said the new outages were added to the effects of earlier damage, that energy workers had come under attack but that none of them was injured, and that repair crews had already begun work despite the threat of further attacks. Earlier Sunday morning, occupation city head Aleksey Kulemzin, as reported by Lenta.ru at 9:20 a.m. Sunday, updated at 9:27 a.m. Sunday (12:20 a.m. and 12:27 a.m. CT if Moscow time), and by Vesti at 8:22 a.m. Sunday (11:22 p.m. CT Saturday if Moscow time), said that all districts of Donetsk were partially without power, and those reports, citing Kulemzin and Donetskenergo, gave city figures of 36,655 subscribers plus 4,700 more disconnected because of network load. NEWS.ru, in its Sunday report on the later Chertkov figures, also said that on Nov 21 energy workers had restored power to all Donetsk subscribers who had been left without electricity by network overloads and emergency disconnections on the evening of Nov 20. An earlier Saturday morning official region-wide remaining total of more than 107,000 subscribers as of 7:00 a.m. Saturday was superseded by the Sunday morning Chertkov figure of more than 279,000 subscribers. Occupation city head Aleksey Kulemzin, as reported by RIA Novosti at 6:12 p.m. Sunday, Nov 22 (9:12 a.m. CT if Moscow time), citing Donetskenergo, the South-West ESK branch, said that 46,400 subscribers remained without electricity in Donetsk because 352 transformer substations in all districts of the city were disconnected, and that restoration work was continuing. That later Sunday city figure was higher than the earlier Sunday morning city figures reported via Lenta.ru and Vesti. No later official region-wide remaining total after the Sunday morning figure of more than 279,000 subscribers was found as of 6:00 PM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (3:00 a.m. Moscow time Monday, Nov 23).
outages.start: Night of Sunday, Nov 22, 2026, local time, for the attack described by occupation officials; other partial outages in the region were already being reported
outages.etr: Occupation government head Andrei Chertkov, as reported by DNR News at 5:45 p.m. Sunday, Nov 22 (8:45 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said restoration of the damaged energy center would take roughly two to three weeks. No official firm restoration time was given for all remaining subscribers.
outages.updated: Nov 22, 2026, occupation government head Andrei Chertkov via DNR News 5:45 p.m. Sunday (= 8:45 a.m. CT if Moscow time) saying restoration of the damaged energy center would take roughly two to three weeks; earlier Sunday morning Chertkov via Kommersant 11:34 a.m. Sunday (= 2:34 a.m. CT if Moscow time), DNR News 11:15 a.m. Sunday (= 2:15 a.m. CT if Moscow time), NEWS.ru 11:25 a.m. Sunday, Moscow 24 11:14 a.m. Sunday, and Vedomosti, on more than 279,000 subscribers remaining without power as of Sunday morning after an overnight attack, with Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Yenakiieve, Debaltseve, Torez, Snizhne, and nearby districts partially unpowered; earlier Sunday morning occupation city head Aleksey Kulemzin via Lenta.ru and Vesti on Donetsk city figures; earlier Saturday morning official region-wide total of more than 107,000 subscribers, superseded by the Sunday Chertkov figure; occupation city head Aleksey Kulemzin via RIA Novosti 6:12 p.m. Sunday (= 9:12 a.m. CT if Moscow time), citing Donetskenergo, on 46,400 subscribers remaining without power in Donetsk city after 352 transformer substations were disconnected; rechecked 6:00 PM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (3:00 a.m. Moscow time Monday, Nov 23), no later official region-wide remaining total after the Sunday morning figure of more than 279,000 subscribers found

outages.place: Crimea and Sevastopol, including Yevpatoria, Dzhankoy, Bilohirsk, and other districts
outages.cause: A power-capacity shortage after strikes on transmission networks outside the peninsula, according to occupation sources. Krymenergo said consumption-restriction measures continued on Sunday, Nov 22, because of insufficient incoming electricity, and Sevastopolenergo said a temporary restriction regime was in effect on dispatcher orders
outages.affected: Krymenergo, as reported by RIA Novosti Crimea at 4:07 p.m. Sunday, Nov 22, updated at 4:18 p.m. Sunday (7:07 a.m. and 7:18 a.m. CT if Moscow time), and by Krym.Realii at 4:30 p.m. Sunday, said electricity supply had again been restricted in the afternoon in Dzhankoy, Yevpatoria, Bilohirsk, and settlements in six districts of the peninsula, and that the planned time for restoring supply was three hours. Those reports, citing Krymenergo, said the afternoon restrictions affected Dzhankoy and Dzhankoy district, including dozens of city streets and more than 40 settlements; parts of Yevpatoria, on a listed set of streets; Bilohirsk and Bilohirsk district; and parts of the Razdolne, Chornomorske, Kirovske, Pervomaiske, and Bakhchysarai districts. RIA Novosti Crimea, citing Krymenergo, also said there had been an emergency disconnection in Chornomorske district, leaving Vladimirovka and Dalekoe without power, and that Feodosiya was also partly without electricity. The same report said earlier Sunday accounts had described restrictions in Yevpatoria and in the Bakhchysarai, Bilohirsk, Kirovske, Razdolne, and Simferopol districts, outages in the Yalta area because of network accidents, and restrictions in Dzhankoy, Kirovske district, and Feodosiya, and that consumption-restriction measures remained in effect because of insufficient incoming electricity. An earlier Sunday Krymenergo list, reported by RIA Novosti Crimea at 1:30 p.m. Sunday (4:30 a.m. CT if Moscow time), had named parts of Yevpatoria and of the Bakhchysarai, Bilohirsk, Kirovske, Razdolne, and Simferopol districts, also with a planned restoration of about three hours, and still earlier Sunday morning lists were reported at 9:11 a.m., 9:13 a.m., 9:36 a.m., and 9:58 a.m. Sunday (12:11 a.m. to 12:58 a.m. CT if Moscow time). Sevastopolenergo, as reported by RIA Novosti Crimea at 9:45 a.m. Sunday (12:45 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said a temporary electricity-restriction regime had been introduced on the orders of the dispatcher, following a 3-hours-on, 3-hours-off rotation through Sunday evening, and that the energy-system situation in Crimea remained unstable, so the dispatcher could introduce additional restrictions if needed. The later RIA Novosti Crimea report also said a temporary restriction regime remained in effect in Sevastopol on dispatcher orders, with temporary schedules. Occupation sources have said peninsula-wide interruptions began Oct 24, 2026, after strikes on transmission networks outside the peninsula. Later Sunday, Krymenergo, as reported by a Crimea news wire at 5:42 p.m. Sunday, Nov 22 (8:42 a.m. CT if Moscow time), citing the Krymenergoinform channel, said electricity supply had again been restricted in Pervomaiske district, including Pravda, Matveevka, Arbuzovo, Kalinino, Levitanovka, Upornoye, Pshenichnoye, and, in part, Pervomaiske, Stepnoye, Krylovka, Grishino, and Frunze, with an approximate outage time of three hours. Krymenergo, as reported by a Crimea news wire at 7:57 p.m. Sunday (10:57 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said electricity supply had been restricted in Sovietskyi district in Pushkino, Makovka, Novoselovka, Vostochnoye, Dyatlovka, Chapayevka, Novy Mir, Novonikolayevka, Kolomenka, and Krasnogvardeyskoye, also with an approximate outage time of three hours. No official customer count was given. No official notice that the general deficit-related restrictions had been lifted was found as of 6:00 PM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (3:00 a.m. Moscow time Monday, Nov 23).

outages.affected: UNE's Sunday bulletin, published by Granma at 10:11 a.m. Cuba time Sunday, Nov 22 (9:11 a.m. CT) and also reported by Directorio Cubano at 8:32 a.m. Sunday, said service had been affected by a generation-capacity deficit throughout all 24 hours on Saturday, Nov 21, and that the affectation continued through the early morning, with a maximum affectation of 1,778 MW recorded at 6:50 p.m. Cuba time Saturday (5:50 p.m. CT Saturday). It said solar-photovoltaic parks produced 3,474 MWh on Saturday, with a maximum of 540 MW delivered in the midday period. At 6:00 a.m. Cuba time Sunday (5:00 a.m. CT), the bulletin said SEN availability was 1,037 MW against demand of 2,255 MW, with 1,220 MW affected. For the midday period it estimated an affectation of 1,200 MW. UNE estimated that unit 2 of CTE Santa Cruz would enter for the evening peak with 80 MW, and it forecast availability of 1,117 MW against a maximum demand of 2,800 MW, a deficit of 1,683 MW, and, if those conditions held, an affectation of 1,713 MW at the peak. The bulletin said units 1 and 2 of CTE Santa Cruz and unit 2 of CTE Felton were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, unit 5 of CTE Renté, and unit 1 of CTE Felton were in maintenance, with thermal-generation limitations of 423 MW. CiberCuba, in a page updated at 12:12 p.m. Cuba time Sunday (11:12 a.m. CT), presented the same official UNE Sunday figures, said there was no total collapse of the national grid recorded, and continued to show local Havana circuit reports during the late morning. CiberCuba, in a page updated at 6:14 p.m. Cuba time Sunday (5:14 p.m. CT), still presented the same official UNE Sunday morning forecast of a 1,713 MW evening-peak affectation and said there was no total collapse of the national grid recorded. outages.cause: Planned electricity restrictions that Tavanir said began Sunday, Nov 22, 2026, because fuel shortages were disrupting power generation
outages.affected: Iran International, in a report dated 1:17 p.m. GMT Sunday, Nov 22 (7:17 a.m. CT), said scheduled power cuts had resumed across Iran, disrupting homes, businesses, and schools. It said people in Tehran, Isfahan, Shiraz, Mashhad, Yazd, Kermanshah, and Ardabil reported hours-long outages, often without notice, in messages sent to Iran International on Sunday, and that the disruptions had also affected water supplies and internet access. The report said Mohammad Allahdad, chief executive of state electricity company Tavanir, announced Saturday that residential and commercial power restrictions would begin November 22 because of fuel shortages at power plants, and that outages could last two hours every other day, increasing to two hours daily if temperatures fall further. RFE/RL, in a report dated midnight CET Sunday, Nov 22 (5:00 p.m. CT Saturday), said the cuts started Nov 22 and quoted Allahdad telling state television that the outages are expected to last up to two hours a day depending on location. Nour News, in a report dated 8:09 a.m. Iran time Sunday, Nov 22, or 1 Azar 1405 (10:39 p.m. CT Saturday), and Eghtesad Online, in a report dated 8:29 a.m. Iran time Sunday (10:59 p.m. CT Saturday) that cited Nour News, said planned electricity restrictions began today and, citing the Tavanir chief executive, that the new restrictions may take the form of a two-hour outage over two days, or a maximum of two hours each day, that the timing is not fixed and may change with network conditions, and that customers would be informed through the Bargh-e Man system and app, the Bale messenger app, and text messages. Tavanir had announced on Saturday, Nov 21, that planned electricity restrictions on households and businesses would begin on Sunday, Nov 22, because fuel shortages were disrupting power generation, according to Iran International in a report dated 5:11 p.m. GMT Saturday, Nov 21 (11:11 a.m. CT), and to RFE/RL. Anar News, in a report updated at 12:05 a.m. UTC Sunday, Nov 22 (6:05 p.m. CT Saturday), citing BBC Persian, also said planned power outages began in Iran on Sunday, Nov 22, because of fuel shortages at power plants. No official customer count was given in those reports. No official nationwide remaining-customer count was found as of 6:00 PM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (3:30 a.m. Iran time Monday, Nov 23).

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. Drop Site News, in a Nov 20, 2026 report from Khartoum, said a particularly intense wave of drone strikes at the end of October and into November targeting power stations, fuel supplies, and electricity infrastructure had brought the country's power grid to the brink of collapse, and that two weeks after the wave of attacks, major substations remained out of service. Shaker Ismail, an engineer with the Sudanese Electricity Company, told Drop Site that repairing some of the country's most important power facilities could take months or longer, that high-capacity transformers and digital control systems had been damaged, and that replacement transformers must be manufactured to order abroad. Ismail said the Um Dabakir thermal power plant in White Nile State was badly damaged in an Oct 29 strike and forced to shut down, and that the Al-Markhiyat substation west of Omdurman was put out of service after an Oct 27 strike; he said affected areas continued to experience prolonged outages and scheduled power cuts as of this week. The report said the Sudan Electricity Holding Company and Ministry of Energy had yet to publicly announce the restoration of the major facilities damaged in the attacks. A United Nations report published Nov 17, issued in Geneva and posted on the UN in Sudan website, said that in just over two weeks between Oct 20 and Nov 4, 29 drone strikes, attributed to the Rapid Support Forces, hit electricity facilities and fuel stations across 11 states, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. An earlier Al Jazeera Nov 15 feature said there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day, and, citing The Associated Press, said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found as of 6:00 PM CT Sunday, Nov 22.
